messages:
Kai (Sales): quick heads-up — Acme POC blocking on observability. Two things: 1) they can't find trace IDs in Redwood Console to match their req ids, 2) Splunk isn't getting any logs from our forwarder. Also they reported intermittent 429s on embeddings during batch import. Can eng swarm?

Jordan (SRE): on it. do we have an example request + headers from Acme? need their client-side req id and a sample of the 429 response.

Maya R (Eng-ML): I grabbed a sample from their packet capture earlier: header was `X-Acme-ReqID: req_20250310_9a`. They proxy through an API gateway which rewrites some headers. If the gateway strips our `x-rw-trace-id` we won't link traces.

Alex M (DevEx): shortlist steps — 1) confirm inbound header mapping in Private/Reserved config, 2) enable trace propagation, 3) verify Console trace search, 4) validate Splunk HEC settings.

Jordan (SRE): @Alex M can you paste the exact config snippet we recommended?

Alex M (DevEx): sure — put this into the runtime/observability block (Private/Dedicated):

```yaml
observability:
  trace_propagation: true
  inbound_trace_headers:
    - "x-acme-reqid"
  export:
    splunk:
      enabled: true
      hec_token: "<redacted>"
      endpoint: "https://splunk.example.com:8088/services/collector"
```

Alex M (DevEx): also ensure the gateway forwards the header with same casing or add mapping rule. Our parser normalizes headers but if gateway converts `X-Acme-ReqID` -> `x-acme-reqid` that's fine. If it removes it, we lose linkage.

Kai (Sales): they say gateway is Envoy with header-sanitization rules — can we recommend a workaround if they can't change Envoy quickly?

Maya R (Eng-ML): workaround: we can accept a query param as fallback — add `observability.inbound_trace_params: ["trace_id", "reqid"]` in config. Not ideal but works while they update Envoy.

Jordan (SRE): regarding Splunk — logs were failing because the HEC token was using the old shard index. Ask them to check Console -> Integrations -> Log Exporters -> Splunk and ensure the token + index match. Also check network egress from the runtime to Splunk IPs.

Kai (Sales): they shared a failure snippet for the Splunk forwarder: `POST /services/collector 403`

Alex M (DevEx): 403 = bad HEC token/permissions. If they see 403, rotate token or create a new HEC token with `index` write permission and update our `hec_token`. After update restart forwarder or trigger config reload in Console.

Jordan (SRE): embedding 429s — sample response they sent: `{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":12}`. Looks like client-side burst exceeded the per-project embeddings rate. We can bump quota for the Dedicated/Reserved pool or suggest exponential backoff.

Maya R (Eng-ML): For quick mitigation set client to `concurrency: 4` and add jittered backoff. Long term we can raise the embeddings concurrency cap for the POC account. Ping ops if they need temporary bump.

Kai (Sales): I'm coordinating with Acme on Envoy changes; they asked for an exact trace look-up example to hand to their SREs.

Jordan (SRE): give them this — after we map inbound header, you can find the trace in Console by searching the value. Example query: `trace_id: req_20250310_9a` or search logs: `request_id:req_20250310_9a`. Also our internal header is `x-rw-trace-id` — we append `x-rw-trace-id: xrw::<hex>` to logs.

Alex M (DevEx): sample curl to reproduce (ask Acme to run from their gateway):

```bash
curl -i \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" \
  -H "X-Acme-ReqID: req_20250310_9a" \
  -d '{"model":"text-embed-3","input":["a","b"]}' \
  https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/embeddings
```

Alex M (DevEx): in the response headers we echo `X-RW-TRACE-ID: xrw:4f3a2f...` (if trace propagation enabled). Ask them to provide that value if present.

Jordan (SRE): if they don't see `X-RW-TRACE-ID` we either didn't enable propagation or a proxy stripped it. To debug quickly: tail the runtime log and grep for their req id: `grep req_20250310_9a /var/log/redwood/runtime.log` — you should see lines like:

```
2025-03-10T12:03:22.881Z INFO request_id=req_20250310_9a model=text-embed-3 x_rw_trace=xrw:4f3a2f status=200 tokens=0
```

Jordan (SRE): if that line appears but Console doesn't show the trace, check the trace collector service health and the Console ingestion pipeline (Console -> Observability -> Ingestion). I just checked and ingestion showed a 5 minute delay this morning on a different cluster, but it recovered.

Maya R (Eng-ML): added a quick regex we use to map Acme reqid to internal trace id in case they want to automate: `s/req_([0-9a-f_]+)/trace:\1/` — internal mapping script can annotate logs.

Kai (Sales): perfect. I'll relay steps to Acme and ask them to run the curl and tail logs. Also requesting temporary embeddings quota bump.

Jordan (SRE): I'll open a short ops ticket to bump embeddings concurrency for the POC for 48h. Leaving note to revert after.

Alex M (DevEx): docs links I shared previously: https://docs.redwood.ai/observability/trace-propagation and https://docs.redwood.ai/integrations/splunk-hec — send these to their SREs.

Kai (Sales): thanks everyone. I'll update after they run the curl. :thumbsup:


deploy-bot: deployment rtime/observability-config updated by Alex M at 2025-03-10T12:20:00Z :white_check_mark:

Jordan (SRE): follow-up: Acme confirmed they saw `X-RW-TRACE-ID: xrw:4f3a2f` in the response after config change and Splunk HEC was updated; logs now present. embeddings 429 also resolved after temporary bump. Closing swarm unless anyone objects.

Kai (Sales): closing on our side — will monitor usage. Thanks all. :party:"
